text:
Ravi Shah: heads up -- holding tonight's runtime roll to v3.4.0. Deploybot flagged a compatibility mismatch with SDK signing tests in canary. Please triage.

deploybot: automated: release_hold SET on runtime:v3.4.0 reason=sdk-signature-mismatch tests_failed=4/60 canary_region=us-west

Maya Li: which SDKs affected? python or ts? any minimal repro?

Ethan Brooks: repro for python sdk 3.0.0: header canonicalization change causes signature verification to fail on a subset of embedding requests. Repro snippet:
```
python infra/canary/run.py --target runtime:v3.4.0 --suite signing --region us-west
```

Maya Li: ok. options are: 1) pin runtime to older behavior (breaks new serializer), 2) gate by SDK version, or 3) roll runtime with backward-compatible shim.

Ravi Shah: prefer gate by SDK tag to avoid regressing correctness. Proposal: route SDK>=3.0.1 to v3.4.0, SDK<3.0.1 to v3.3.7. Start with 2% rollout in us-west. Fallback = v3.3.7.

ops-bot: deploybot command accepted: create-route-rule runtime:v3.4.0 condition=sdk_version>=3.0.1 rollout=2% region=us-west

Ethan Brooks: running signed-request fuzz on the 2% cohort now, will post results in 20m.

Maya Li: adding compatibility note to release notes: "Runtime v3.4.0 requires SDK >= 3.0.1 for embedding signature canonicalization."

Ravi Shah: rollback criteria: canary error rate >1.5% OR p95 latency increase >120ms for 15m -> rollback to v3.3.7 and open incident. I've updated the release runbook.

deploybot: canary update: 58/60 checks passed, two intermittent signature failures. tagging @sdk-team for patch release.

Ethan Brooks: looks like the flaky cases are due to header-ordering in multipart requests. SDK patch targeted for 3.0.1 in ~35m. Holding final lift until publish and a clean smoke in us-west.

Ravi Shah: thanks. keep thread updated. once SDK 3.0.1 is live and canary clean, we'll remove hold and continue rollout. :white_check_mark:
